narrativeReportMd:
# PaymentNotice R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`PaymentNotice` remains the same concrete resource, but local R6 changes introduce one hard R4-to-R6 instance break and several R6-to-R4 round-trip risks. The main hard break is the replacement of `PaymentNotice.provider` with `PaymentNotice.reporter`; R4 instances that contain `provider` will fail strict R6 validation unless transformed.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4/R6 core StructureDefinitions plus directly related terminology and package metadata. Inherited base-resource changes are explicitly out of scope and are not counted as PaymentNotice findings.

## Main migration themes
Migration code should rename `provider` to `reporter` with human review of semantics, handle `payment` becoming optional in R6, preserve R6 `statusReason` when downgrading to R4, and review conformance expectations for `paymentStatus` because its binding strength increased from `example` to `preferred`.

## Highest-impact findings
The provider-to-reporter rename is the only local hard R4-to-R6 validation break found. The optionalization of `payment` is not a forward validation break, but it is a high R6-to-R4 representability risk because R4 requires the payment reference.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for deciding whether R4 `provider` values truly mean the R6 `reporter`, for backfilling or rejecting R6 notices without `payment`, and for confirming terminology impact for `paymentStatus` with a complete R6 terminology source.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 changes appear aimed at clearer workflow semantics and broader lifecycle coverage, but the rename could have been less disruptive if the old element had been retained or deprecated alongside the new element.

## Follow-up analysis
Base `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes, PaymentNotice SearchParameters, and terminology package changes should be reviewed by their own artifact reports.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `PaymentNotice` has a local hard break because R4 `provider` was replaced by R6 `reporter`. The main migration concerns are element rename/semantic drift, R6 notices that omit the formerly required `payment`, and R6-only `statusReason`; terminology confidence for `paymentStatus` is limited by missing local R6 CodeSystem/expansion evidence.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Forward R4-to-R6 migration is mostly straightforward except for `provider`: strict R6 parsers will reject the old element name, and implementers should decide whether each R4 provider really is the party reporting the notice. Backward R6-to-R4 conversion has greater data-loss risk because R6 can omit `payment` and can carry `statusReason`, neither of which maps cleanly into base R4 without either deriving data or using extensions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local element/cardinality/type changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is medium for terminology impact because the local ValueSets did not include expansions and the R6 core package did not include the `paymentstatus` CodeSystem resource even though the R6 ValueSet references that external system.

findings.title: PaymentNotice.provider was replaced by PaymentNotice.reporter

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `provider` 0..1, referencing Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization.

semanticText.definition: The practitioner who is responsible for the services rendered to the patient.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances could carry `PaymentNotice.provider` to identify the practitioner or organization responsible for the services rendered.

newState.summary: R6 has optional `reporter` 0..1 with the same reference target set, but no `provider` element.

semanticText.definition: The party who reports the payment notice.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 replaces the old element name with `PaymentNotice.reporter`. The type and cardinality match the old element, but the definition now emphasizes the party reporting the notice rather than the party responsible for rendered services.

facts.note: `provider` is absent from the R6 PaymentNotice snapshot and differential.
`reporter` is new in R6 at the same parent with matching cardinality and target profiles.

facts.oldValue: The practitioner who is responsible for the services rendered to the patient.
facts.newValue: The party who reports the payment notice.
facts.note: The rename is accompanied by a semantic clarification/broadening.
Supporting evidence only; SearchParameters are outside this resource report's primary scope.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `reporter` element appears in the same location, has the same 0..1 cardinality, same Reference target profiles, same short label, and matching workflow/w5 mappings as the removed R4 `provider`; the local SearchParameter rename corroborates the match.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct element-name break. A strict R6 validator or generated R6 model will reject the R4 `provider` property as unknown, and R6 `reporter` is likewise unknown to strict R4 processors unless transformed. Runtime APIs, generated accessors, JSONPath/FHIRPath expressions, search clients, and mapping code that reference `provider` must be updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The business risk is misattribution: the old value may identify the provider responsible for services, while the new element is the reporter of the notice. Those can be different parties in payment workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that the element identifies the party reporting the payment notice, not necessarily the care or service provider.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `PaymentNotice.provider` in the base resource with a clarified reporter-focused definition, aliases, and deprecation guidance rather than replacing the element name.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying the reporting-party semantics is a reasonable R6 goal, but the direct element rename creates a hard validation/API break while the type, cardinality, and target set stayed the same. Because the old path could likely have been retained with clearer normative text and migration guidance, the level of breakage appears probably avoidable from the local evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain `PaymentNotice.provider` as 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|Organization) and revise its definition to identify the party reporting the notice, with alias/deprecation notes explaining the legacy name. A second possible design would add `reporter` while retaining deprecated `provider`, but that has worse duplicate-representation risk. Keeping the old path would preserve most R4-valid instances while still making the R6 semantic correction explicit, at the cost of carrying a nonoptimal element name and reviewing data where the service provider is not the reporter.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances with no duplicate field, but leaves a misleading legacy name and requires semantic review where provider and reporter differ.

evidence.quote: The practitioner who is responsible for the services rendered to the patient.
The party who reports the payment notice.

evidence.detail: The R4 search expression is `PaymentNotice.provider`; the R6 counterpart is `PaymentNotice.reporter`.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are minimal fragments focused on the renamed element while preserving other required PaymentNotice fields. The migration example assumes the old provider is also the reporting party; implementations should verify that assumption.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the R4 `provider` element and introduces `reporter` in the same structural slot. The mechanical shape strongly indicates a rename, but the definition changes from responsibility for rendered services to reporting the notice, which can be a real workflow distinction. This will surprise implementers because simple code generation treats it as delete/add, while safe migration may require business semantics, not only a property rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `provider` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6 because `provider` is not an allowed R6 element. Conversely, an R6 instance containing `reporter` is not valid base R4. Generated models lose the old accessor and gain a new one; FHIRPath, search, transformation rules, and persistence schemas using `provider` need explicit updates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, transform `PaymentNotice.provider` to `PaymentNotice.reporter` only when the source value identifies the party reporting the notice. If the source value specifically identifies the service provider and a different reporter is known, map the reporter separately and preserve provider semantics via an extension or workflow-specific related data. Regression tests should cover provider present, provider absent, and provider distinct from reporter.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change likely improves clarity, but a backward-compatible path existed: keep `provider` and add `reporter`, or keep the element name while changing narrative guidance. Those alternatives would preserve instance compatibility but leave systems with either duplicate elements or a historically misleading name.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for data sets where the provider responsible for services is not necessarily the reporter of the payment notice.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `PaymentNotice.provider` and R6 `PaymentNotice.reporter` have the same cardinality and reference target set, but the old wire element is gone and the definition shifted from the party responsible for rendered services to the party reporting the notice. An R4 instance carrying `provider` is therefore old-valid/new-invalid in R6, and clients or servers using the related `provider` search parameter must move to `reporter`. Because provider and reporter can be different parties in payment workflows, migration is not always a safe mechanical rename; it can affect financial attribution and audit meaning.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.provider: 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|Organization), definition is the practitioner responsible for services rendered.

R6 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.reporter: 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|Organization), definition is the party who reports the payment notice; no R6 PaymentNotice.provider element is present.
SearchParameter changed from PaymentNotice-provider expression PaymentNotice.provider in R4 to PaymentNotice-reporter expression PaymentNotice.reporter in R6.
R4 PaymentNotice metadata: FMM 2, standards status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral rather than a strong stability guarantee, but it also is not the very-low-FMM case. The direct wire/search break and billing attribution risk drive the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances with `provider` are not base-valid R6, generated accessors and FHIRPath/search expressions change, and R6 `reporter` is not representable as the old R4 element without a transform.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base R6 design appears plausible. R6 could have retained `provider` as a deprecated legacy element while adding `reporter`, or kept the old wire name if the intended role was the same and clarified the definition. The tradeoff is either duplicate/conflicting same-resource representations or carrying a misleading legacy name, but both would better preserve R4 data and expose the semantic distinction for review.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high impact and less-breaking-alternative judgment are consistent with the independent path-level assessment, though the semantic shift means some migrations need role review rather than a blind rename.

findings.title: PaymentNotice.payment is no longer required in R6

oldState.summary: R4 required a payment reference: 1..1 Reference(PaymentReconciliation).

semanticText.definition: A reference to the payment which is the subject of this notice.
semanticText.requirements: Need to identify the actual payment.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every base R4 PaymentNotice had to identify the PaymentReconciliation that was the subject of the notice.

newState.summary: R6 makes the same payment reference optional: 0..1 Reference(PaymentReconciliation).

semanticText.definition: A reference to the payment which is the subject of this notice.
semanticText.requirements: Need to identify the actual payment.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows a PaymentNotice to be valid without the payment reference, even though the requirements text still says the actual payment needs to be identified.

facts.note: Only requiredness changed; the target resource did not.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Lowering minimum cardinality is not a forward R4-to-R6 validation break because any R4 instance with the required `payment` still satisfies R6. It is, however, a high backward-conversion risk: a valid R6 PaymentNotice may omit `payment` and then cannot satisfy base R4 without deriving or inventing a PaymentReconciliation reference. Generated code and business logic that assumed a non-null payment reference must also change for R6.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Payment reconciliation workflows often depend on the payment reference for matching, auditing, and de-duplication. Missing payment references can create operational ambiguity even when R6 validation allows them.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow notices to exist before a PaymentReconciliation reference is known, or allow status-only notices such as drafts/cancellations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable because lowering `payment` from 1..1 to 0..1 preserves R4-valid instances; the concern is R6-to-R4 downgrade and nullable-runtime handling.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing a PaymentNotice without a payment reference is a plausible R6 modeling goal for draft, preliminary, or cancellation workflows. This is not an R4-to-R6 instance break because every R4 instance that satisfied the required `payment` element remains structurally valid in R6, although the unchanged requirements text leaves some rationale uncertainty.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules, no less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed: the R6 change relaxes cardinality rather than rejecting old content. Keeping `payment` mandatory would reduce R6-to-R4 downgrade gaps and preserve a stronger business invariant, but it would also block the apparent R6 goal of representing payment notices before a specific PaymentReconciliation is available.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6 gains flexibility for notices without a known PaymentReconciliation, but older-version conversion may require derivation, rejection, or non-base extensions.

evidence.detail: The R4 target profile is PaymentReconciliation.
The R6 target profile remains PaymentReconciliation.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example is valid with respect to the changed `payment` cardinality but would fail R4 because `payment` is mandatory there. The migration example is only safe if the payment reference can be derived from trusted source data.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes `PaymentNotice.payment` from required to optional. This is backward-compatible for existing R4 instances but changes a core invariant many systems may have relied on: the notice no longer necessarily points to the PaymentReconciliation it is about.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid solely because of this cardinality relaxation. The break is in the other direction: R6-valid content can be impossible to serialize as conformant R4 because R4 requires the reference. Runtime code generated from R4 may also assume `payment` is always populated and fail or misbehave on R6 data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R6 consumers should treat `payment` as nullable and test missing-reference cases. R6-to-R4 transforms must either derive a real PaymentReconciliation reference, reject/quarantine the record for manual handling, or use a non-base extension/profile strategy that will not be valid as plain R4. Do not invent placeholder references unless the receiving workflow explicitly permits them.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The flexibility may be useful for draft or status-change notices, but relaxing base cardinality was not the only design path. A profile, invariant warning, or explicit absence-reason extension could have preserved the base R4 shape while documenting exceptional cases; the tradeoff is less universal support for payment-less notices.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review downstream reconciliation rules before accepting R6 PaymentNotice resources that omit `payment`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 relaxes `PaymentNotice.payment` from required to optional while leaving the PaymentReconciliation target and requirements text unchanged. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break: every valid R4 instance already has `payment` and still satisfies the R6 cardinality. The real compatibility issue is downstream and reverse-directional: valid R6 notices may omit the payment reference, cannot be losslessly downgraded to base R4, and R6 code can no longer assume a non-null payment link. That is meaningful for reconciliation and audit workflows, but it looks proportionate if R6 intended to support draft, cancellation, or pre-reconciliation notices.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.payment: min 1, max 1, Reference(PaymentReconciliation).
R6 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.payment: min 0, max 1, Reference(PaymentReconciliation).
Both R4 and R6 keep the definition as a reference to the payment subject of the notice and requirements text saying the actual payment needs to be identified.
R4 PaymentNotice metadata: FMM 2, standards status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 2/trial-use gives neutral stability pressure. The centrality of the payment reference creates real business migration concern, but the lower maturity makes the relaxation easier to accept if it supports legitimate R6 workflow flexibility.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen: there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break, but R6 instances without `payment` cannot satisfy base R4 and generated R6 models/business logic must handle null.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `payment` required, or adding a conditional invariant that requires it except for specific statuses, would reduce downgrade and nullability burden. Those alternatives also restrict the apparent R6 goal of allowing a notice before a specific PaymentReconciliation is known, and a conditional rule would add policy complexity. No clearly superior less-breaking base design is evident.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies no forward hard break and real R6-to-R4/nullability risk, but its high overall impact overstates this as a direct R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findings.title: R6 adds optional PaymentNotice.statusReason

oldState.summary: R4 had no `statusReason` element on PaymentNotice.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could represent status but not a base-resource reason for why the status changed, except through extensions or external workflow context.

semanticText.definition: Used to indicate why the status has changed.
semanticText.comment: Implementation guides may consider adding invariants such that if status = cancelled, statusReason SHALL be supplied.
semanticText.requirements: This is used to implement conformance on other elements.

newState.narrativeMd: The new optional string lets R6 instances explain why the PaymentNotice status changed, especially for cancellation workflows.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not invalidate existing R4 PaymentNotice instances when moving forward to R6. The risk is loss or invalidity when moving backward: base R4 has no `statusReason` slot, and strict R4 parsers reject the unknown property unless it is transformed to an extension or omitted.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of a status reason can reduce auditability or cancellation explanation, but it does not by itself change the modifier status code.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide base support for explaining status changes and enable IGs to require a reason for statuses such as cancelled.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable because `statusReason` is an optional additive R6 element that does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding an optional status explanation is a reasonable and low-disruption way to support audit and cancellation workflows. Because the element is optional and additive, it creates no R4-to-R6 base validation break; its compatibility issue is only that populated R6 data has no plain R4 slot.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A cross-version or implementation-specific extension can preserve `statusReason` when converting to R4, but that is a downgrade/backport strategy, not a less-breaking R6 base design. The base R6 design is already forward-compatible for existing R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The base R6 element improves discoverability; R4 downgrade requires an extension, omission, or out-of-band preservation, which is a migration mitigation rather than a base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `PaymentNotice.statusReason` with cardinality 0..1 and type string.
evidence.quote: Used to indicate why the status has changed.

examples.examplesMd: The extension URL in the migration example is illustrative only; production use should use an agreed canonical cross-version extension if one exists.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `statusReason`, an optional summary string explaining why the status changed. This is not an R4-to-R6 break, but it introduces a new information-bearing field that older systems will not understand by default.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Existing R4 instances remain valid with respect to this addition. R6 instances that populate `statusReason` cannot be represented in base R4 as-is; strict R4 JSON validation rejects the unknown member. Tolerant parsers might ignore it, which is a data-loss risk rather than a validation success.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading to R4, map `statusReason` to a well-governed extension or preserve it out-of-band. Test cancellation and entered-in-error examples because R6 implementation guides may choose to make the reason required by profile even though the base resource does not.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 addition is forward-compatible and useful. For older versions, an extension is the natural compatibility bridge; the main tradeoff is discoverability and consistent receiver support.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `PaymentNotice.statusReason` is an optional additive R6 element. It gives R6 instances a base place to explain a status change, especially cancellation, but it does not invalidate any R4 PaymentNotice moving forward to R6. The only compatibility concern is that populated R6 status reasons have no native R4 slot and would need an extension, omission, or out-of-band preservation when downgrading.
keyEvidence: R4 PaymentNotice has no statusReason element.
R6 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.statusReason: 0..1 string, summary=true, definition says it indicates why the status changed.
R6 comment says implementation guides may consider invariants requiring statusReason when status is cancelled.
R4 PaymentNotice metadata: FMM 2, standards status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, and the additive optional shape leaves little stability burden to weigh.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: forward R4-to-R6 instances remain valid; reverse conversion of populated `statusReason` needs an extension or loses explanatory/audit text.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because the element is optional and additive. A cross-version extension can help R4 downgrade, but that is a migration/backport mechanism rather than a better R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report's evidence and reverse-loss note are sound, but treating the additive change as medium impact overstates the standards-design concern.

findings.title: PaymentNotice.paymentStatus binding strengthened from example to preferred

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 ValueSet includes the external system `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/paymentstatus`; the local R4 CodeSystem contains `paid` and `cleared`.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the value set was illustrative only; conformant instances could use any CodeableConcept coding without even a preferred-code expectation.

newState.summary: R6 binding strength is `preferred` to the same value set canonical.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet compose still includes `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/paymentstatus`, but the R6 core package did not contain a local CodeSystem-payment-status.json for direct code comparison.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, implementations are expected to prefer the payment-status value set where suitable, although non-value-set codes are still not invalid solely because the binding is preferred.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR `preferred` bindings are stronger conformance guidance than `example` bindings, but they do not make out-of-set CodeableConcepts invalid in the same way a `required` binding would. The practical risk is warning-level validation, implementation policy changes, enum preference assumptions, or profile authors treating the preferred set as a de facto requirement.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Payment-status code interpretation affects financial workflow state, but the binding remains non-required in the base resource.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve interoperability by encouraging common payment status codes while still allowing alternatives.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the binding at `example` strength and add narrative or best-practice guidance recommending the payment-status codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Encouraging shared payment-status coding is a reasonable interoperability goal, and `preferred` is still non-invalidating in the base resource. A less disruptive path exists, but it would not provide the same computable signal to validators, tooling, and profile authors, so the limited conformance churn appears probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would leave `PaymentNotice.paymentStatus` bound at `example` strength and use comments, implementation notes, or profile guidance to recommend the standard payment-status codes. That preserves old validator expectations and avoids new preferred-binding warnings, but only partially meets the R6 goal because the recommendation is less machine-readable and less consistently enforced across tooling.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids validator-warning and policy churn, but materially weakens computable interoperability guidance and is easier for implementations to ignore.

evidence.detail: The R4 package includes local codes `paid` and `cleared`; no R6 local CodeSystem-payment-status.json was present in the R6 core package.

examples.examplesMd: The `oldValidNewInvalidJson` fragment is not expected to become hard invalid solely from the preferred binding; it illustrates an R4 pattern that may draw R6 validator warnings or local policy review.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 strengthens `paymentStatus` terminology guidance from an example binding to a preferred binding. This does not prohibit local codes, but it raises the interoperability expectation and can affect validators, quality checks, and generated enum-helper behavior.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a hard base validation break: `preferred` bindings are recommendations, not required membership constraints. The compatibility effect is mainly conformance/runtime policy. Systems that previously ignored the example ValueSet may start seeing warnings or may need to include at least one `paid`/`cleared` coding alongside local codes if they want to satisfy preferred-code expectations.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review `paymentStatus` coding practices. Where the local status can be mapped to the standard payment-status system, add the standard coding while preserving local codings if needed. Do not drop local codes unless a reliable ConceptMap/business mapping exists. Confirm behavior with the validator used by the target R6 environment.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The working group could have left the binding as `example` and relied on narrative guidance, which would avoid warning churn. The chosen `preferred` strength is still a relatively compatible way to improve consistency because it stops short of `extensible` or `required`.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology confidence is medium because no expansion was present and the R6 core package did not include the referenced paymentstatus CodeSystem resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `PaymentNotice.paymentStatus` keeps the same CodeableConcept shape and value set canonical while the binding strength increases from `example` to `preferred`. That can create validator warnings or policy pressure to use the common payment-status codes, but it still does not make out-of-set codings invalid in the base resource. For this path, the change is useful interoperability guidance rather than a hard compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.paymentStatus binding strength is example to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/payment-status.
R6 StructureDefinition PaymentNotice.paymentStatus binding strength is preferred to the same value set canonical.
Both R4 and R6 ValueSet-payment-status compose include http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/paymentstatus.
R4 package CodeSystem-payment-status contains paid and cleared; the base binding remains non-required.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. Because the binding remains non-required, the maturity level does not turn warning-level conformance pressure into a material breaking concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: preferred binding may produce validation warnings or influence profiles/tooling, but it is not old-valid/new-invalid for CodeableConcept content.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less disruptive design would keep `example` strength and add prose recommending the payment-status codes. That would avoid warning/policy churn but materially weakens the computable signal that shared codes are preferred, so it is only a partial alternative.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's low-impact assessment and partial less-breaking alternative are consistent with the fresh review.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and `abstract=false` are unchanged. The metadata status changed from draft to active and is recorded as a notable non-breaking change.
Existing local element datatypes and reference types are unchanged. The only type-bearing addition is the new `statusReason` string element, covered separately.

Existing reference target profiles are unchanged: request/response still target Resource, payment still targets PaymentReconciliation, recipient still targets Organization, and payee plus provider/reporter use Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization.
No local PaymentNotice invariants were added, removed, or strengthened. Differences in inherited `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraints are excluded as base-artifact changes.
No local fixed values, pattern values, or default values were found on PaymentNotice elements in either version.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex-style value limit changes were found.
The local modifier element `PaymentNotice.status` remains a modifier with the same reason. R6 explicitly sets many `isModifier=false` defaults, but that is not a material change.
Existing local summary flags are stable: status, created, payment, recipient, and amount remain summary elements. The new `statusReason` summary flag is handled in its own finding.
No local PaymentNotice slicing or slice changes were found.
No resourceType/canonical serialization change or choice-element representation change was found. Serialization breaks are limited to the local element rename and additions covered in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The artifact remains the same concrete resource with the same canonical URL and type. Status metadata affects maturity/ballot interpretation, not instance element validity by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance processes may treat the R6 ballot artifact as more mature, but this does not remove the need to account for the local breaking element changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required status binding points to the R6 fm-status ValueSet version with the same local codes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both local fm-status CodeSystems contain the same four codes: `active`, `cancelled`, `draft`, and `entered-in-error`. The binding remains required, so no new local code-membership break was found from the available terminology files.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that pin ValueSet versions should update from `fm-status|4.0.1` to `fm-status|6.0.0-ballot4`, but code values appear stable in the local package evidence.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records default false flags on many local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omitted many `mustSupport=false`/`isModifier=false` values that R6 records explicitly. These are not a behavioral strengthening because false is the default semantics for base element definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators that diff raw JSON may report noise unless they normalize absent false values and explicit false values.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `PaymentNotice.language` inherits a binding change from preferred `ValueSet/languages` to required `ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4`. This may be important for validators, but it is inherited from the base resource and should be assessed by the Resource/base-artifact report.

Several snapshot differences, including `dom-3` expression text, contained-resource comments, extension constraints, and `modifierExtension` summary behavior, are inherited DomainResource/Element/Extension changes rather than local PaymentNotice changes.

The local R6 ValueSet references `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/paymentstatus`, but the R6 core package did not include the corresponding CodeSystem or expansion. A terminology-focused review should confirm code stability and mapping guidance.
The local element rename has a matching search parameter rename from R4 `provider` to R6 `reporter`. Search API compatibility should be assessed in SearchParameter-specific analysis.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or change-note artifact was available in the local inputs, so justification and rename intent were inferred from the computable definitions and related SearchParameters.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official R6 ballot change log, Jira issue, or generated diff for PaymentNotice.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local ValueSets did not include expansions. For `paymentStatus`, the R6 package also lacked the referenced `CodeSystem-payment-status.json`, limiting certainty about added/removed codes beyond the unchanged ValueSet compose system URL.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an R6 terminology package/server expansion for `ValueSet/payment-status` and compare it with R4 including ConceptMaps if available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The new artifact is a current R6 ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`), not necessarily a final published R6 release. Findings reflect this local build only.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final R6 package when published.
